scope: Theorem 12.2 (Two bounded-box material tests) of the manuscript “Incompressible Box Transport and Finite Computation” (preprints/Incompressible-Box-Transport-and-Finite-Computation-October-6-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2505dc09d3f2c24b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 51. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a positive computable viscosity ν. A deterministic one-tape machine and finite input effectively determine each of the following general body forces on [0, ∞) × R3. Both have zero initial velocity, a unique global smooth velocity in (38), and constructed pressure zero. 1. The force and velocity have one fixed compact spatial support, all mixed derivatives bounded, and period one for t ≥ 1. The particle from 0 enters (−5, −2) × (−1, 2) × (−1, 1) exactly when the machine halts. 2. The force and velocity have one fixed compact spatial support and, for all k ≥ 0 and spatial multi-indices α, satisfy ∥∂k t ∂α x u(t)∥∞ + ∥∂k t ∂α x f(t)∥∞ ≤ Ck,α(1 + t)−1−k . (40) The particle from (2, 0, 0) enters (−1/2, 3/2) × (−1/2, 3/2) × (−1/2, 1/2) exactly when the machine halts. In particular f ∈ L2([0, ∞); Hm(R3)) for every integer m ≥ 0. The supports and constants may depend on the machine and input. The labels and observers do not. All force derivatives admit evaluation to any prescribed rational error by a finite program.
